Messages.Author: brandons...@yahoo.com
Messages.Body:
Nightstick [LotN:U]
Cardtype: Equipment
Cost: 1 pool
Melee weapon.
Strike: strength+1 damage. Or strike: prevent 3 damage [to this
striking minion] from the opposing minion's next hand or melee weapon
strike this round (including any currently-resolving hand or melee
weapon strike). Only usable once each round.

Lam Into [TR:C]
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Fortitude/Potence/Vicissitude
Requires an anarch. Do not replace until after combat. Strike: hand
strike or use a melee weapon strike.
[for] This strike is at +1 damage, with an optional maneuver.
[pot] This strike is at +2 damage.
[vic] This strike is at +1 damage, with an optional press. If another
round of combat occurs, range is automatically close.

Two questions:
1) If I play Lamb Into as a strike using Nightstick, can I use it with
the Strike: Prevent 3 damage to do damage and prevent?
2) Do you have to announce which of the two Nightstick strikes you are
using as you announce that you are striking with a Nightstick via Lamb
Into?

Thanks,
Brandon

Messages.Author: jcrossn...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Note: the card is "Lam Into", not "Lamb Into", as your quoted text
supports.

> Two questions:
> 1) If I play Lamb Into as a strike using Nightstick, can I use it with
> the Strike: Prevent 3 damage to do damage and prevent?

No. The damage prevention strike is a specific strike, as is Lam Into,
or any other strike card.

> 2) Do you have to announce which of the two Nightstick strikes you are
> using as you announce that you are striking with a Nightstick via Lamb
> Into?

You would have to declare which option you're using if you had a
choice, but you don't.

Jesse

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <aa50ef18-2fca-4cc7...@c58g2000hsc.googlegroup

s.com>, jcrossn...@gmail.com writes:
>> Two questions:

>> 1) If I play Lam Into as a strike using Nightstick, can I use it with

>> the Strike: Prevent 3 damage to do damage and prevent?
>
>No. The damage prevention strike is a specific strike, as is Lam Into,
>or any other strike card.

Incorrect. Lam Into tells you to Strike: use a melee weapon strike, so
you can any strike provided by the melee weapon.

http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/2c4dc6f9eda1853f
LSJ, replying to Meej asking about Nightstick's prevent damage strike:
***
> Could you use Undead Strength to add damage to it?

You could select the non-damage-dealing strike when using the melee
weapon Nightstick with Undead Strength, sure. As always, adding damage
to a strike that doesn't deal damage has no effect, so the strike still
won't do damage.
***

So you can play it and use the card, but it won't usually do you any
good - you'll just get a Prevent 3 damage strike.

This may be useful if you have a hand stuffed with Undead Strength but
don't actually want to hurt the minion e.g. you've blocked a bounce.

>> 2) Do you have to announce which of the two Nightstick strikes you
>> are using as you announce that you are striking with a Nightstick via

>> Lam Into?

>
>You would have to declare which option you're using if you had a
>choice, but you don't.

Incorrect - you do have the choice, as above, and you would declare it
when you chose your strike.

--
James Coupe

>>> No. The damage prevention strike is a specific strike, as is Lam Into,
>>> or any other strike card.
>>
>> Incorrect. Lam Into tells you to Strike: use a melee weapon strike, so
>> you can any strike provided by the melee weapon.
>>
>
>Hmm, isn't there a generic rule that damage-enhancing effects require
>the strike to be damage-dealing to begin with?

To have any effect, yes. LSJ's quote, and the rest of my post,
explained this - you can play it, it just won't do you any good usually.

The usual examples are:

- Increased Strength on a Shattering Blow - no damage increase
- Increased Strength on a Fractured Armament superior - yes, damage
increase because it has a damage component
- Undead Strength with a Rowan Ring - no damage
- Theft of Vitae by Reverend Blackwood - steal blood, no damage

However, as in the Undead Strength/Rowan Ring case, you can *play*
Undead Strength. It's just going to be useless (except for cycling, and
other such fripperies).

>I don't recall Casino
>Reeds being able to inflict 1 damage while destroying a weapon with
>superior Canine Horde.

Right. The damage special tries to add to non-existent damage, and has
no effect - like Reverend and Theft.
